newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan economic recovery moves "half step forward".
newsitem.headline: Japan economic recovery moves "half step forward".

text.p: Japan's government moved "half a step forward" on Tuesday in assessing the strength of the economy, presenting a positive picture of gradual recovery after a period of sluggishness.
In its monthly report on the state of the economy, the Economic Planning Agency (EPA) chose to omit a previous reference to worrying factors and focussed instead on the bright aspects of the economy.
It also dropped a call contained in past reports for continued easy credit to help the economy along, saying instead the government would try to manage the economy appropriately.

Commenting on the report, an agency official told reporters: "We took half a step forward in evaluating Japan's economic recovery...we're back to where the economy was before the summer sluggishness set in."

The report reiterated that private consumption was continuing to recover gradually, and housing starts were increasing at a rapid pace, fuelling a rise in output. It also noted that the pace of decline in exports was slowing down.

The government's economic policy unit has said for most of this year that Japan's economy was recovering despite some weakness. The latest report kept a familiar reference to phrase about gradual economic recovery but moved an inch forward by deleting the phrase "there are some worrying aspects".

The November report also omitted recommendations on remedies for the economy which had been included in EPA reports since the government announced massive economic stimulus measures in September 1995.

The report deleted specific policies such as the expansion of domestic demand, the resolution of financial institutions' bad loan woes, and continued low interest rates. Instead, it inserted a phrase promising that the government would try to "appropriately manage" the economy.

The EPA official repeatedly stressed that the change in the report's phraseology -- closely watched by markets for signs of any policy shift -- did not imply that the government no longer sought deregulation or easy credit.

"We haven't changed our stance on the policies for the economy. The government is committed to promoting various reforms necessary to strengthen economic recovery and to achieve long term economic stability," he said.

The official added that Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto's new government would likely discuss appropriate measures to promote economic recovery. "We just believe it's not the EPA's role to specify individual policies," he said.
The agency also used more upbeat phrases to describe personal spending, industrial production, imports and the balance of payments.
Industrial production is gradually increasing, the official said, noting that inventory adjustment appeared to be nearly over and production was on the increase.
The downturn in the semiconductor industry is "bottoming out", helping to boost industrial production, he added.

On trade, the report noted that the increase in imports was slowing and the pace of decline in the trade surplus losing steam. "Overseas demand has ceased to become a factor pulling back the economic recovery and private demand has recovered to the earlier pace," the official said.
The government declared in February that the nation's economy had finally come out of the slump that followed the collapse of the "bubble" economy in the early 1990s.

But the EPA had not been able to take its assessment further than a "gradual recovery" since then. Japanese interest rates have been at record low levels for more than a year to promote economic recovery.
